chunks.subject: AP Comparative Government
chunks.title: Q4 Argument Essay (5 points) — Set 1: civil liberties & stability
chunks.content: AP Comparative Government FRQ 4 is the Argument Essay, 5 points across four rows. Row A Claim/Thesis [1]: a defensible thesis establishing a line of reasoning that uses at least one required course concept. Row B Evidence [2]: two pieces of specific, relevant evidence from required course countries tied to a course concept (1 point each). Row C Reasoning [1]: explain how/why the evidence supports the thesis (requires the Row A point). Row D Alternate Perspectives [1]: describe an opposing perspective AND refute, concede, or rebut it (requires the Row A point; merely describing the alternate view is not enough). Set 1 prompt: whether government protections of civil liberties increase or decrease stability in a state, using one or more of democratization, transparency, and rule of law. Common failure: a 'thesis' that only restates the prompt (loses A); presenting an alternate view without refuting/conceding/rebutting it (loses D); evidence not tied to a course concept.

chunks.subject: AP Comparative Government
chunks.title: Q4 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 4A, 5/5
chunks.content: Q4 (Set 1) scored 5/5 (Thesis 1, Evidence 2, Reasoning 1, Alternate 1). Thesis: protections of civil liberties increase stability through transparency. Evidence: UK transparency during Brexit; Iran's media control/hijab enforcement → protests. Reasoning: government honesty builds trust that stabilizes the state. Alternate perspective: acknowledged the 'loss of control/factions' counterargument then rebutted it. Full-credit model for the argument essay.

chunks.subject: AP Comparative Government
chunks.title: Q4 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 4B, 4/5
chunks.content: Q4 (Set 1) scored 4/5 (Thesis 1, Evidence 2, Reasoning 1, Alternate 0). Thesis links protections to stability via transparency and rule of law. Evidence: Russia (rule by law, subjective punishments) and China (media censorship reducing transparency). Reasoning: reduced transparency undermines trust and stability. Lost Row D: presented an alternate argument but offered no rebuttal, refutation, or concession. Illustrates the most common argument-essay miss — describing the counterview without responding to it.

chunks.subject: AP Comparative Government
chunks.title: Q4 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 4C, 2/5
chunks.content: Q4 (Set 1) scored 2/5 (Thesis 0, Evidence 2, Reasoning 0, Alternate 0). Earned both evidence points (UK rule of law protecting civil liberties; Nigeria democratization with low transparency re: MOSOP). Lost the thesis point because the claim referenced 'fundamental principles of a democracy' without using democratization, transparency, or rule of law as the line of reasoning — and because Row A was not earned, Reasoning and Alternate Perspectives were ineligible. Illustrates how a thesis that omits the required course concepts caps the score even with strong evidence.
